entry.title: New Laws Will Lower Costs, Strengthen Education, and Create Opportunity
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening. 

You know, even at a time when Washington, D.C. seems unable to get much of anything done, here in Maine, we're proving once again that people of goodwill can get together and solve problems. Working with people of all parties and with members of the public, we enacted laws this year that will lower costs, make it easier to rent or buy a home, control childcare costs, strengthen education, and above all, create more opportunity for Maine people.

Dozens of laws took effect this week, including the Supplemental Budget. Education, of course, as we know, opens doors of opportunity, so we focused on education. And that's why in 2022, with the support of the Legislature, we made community college free for recent high school grads. That free community college program has made a life-changing difference for thousands of young people in Maine, and that's why I proposed, and the Legislature approved, making it permanent in this Supplemental Budget.

We also raised teacher pay. We banned cell phones bell-to-bell in the public schools. In addition to all those measures, the budget gives $300 checks back to more than 500,000 people in Maine to help offset, in some small way, the cost of gas, goods, and groceries that are increasing every day because of circumstances we can't control—things like the war in Iran and national tariffs.

The budget builds on my Administration's historic investments in housing, creating more than 400 new affordable homes for families all across Maine. Other laws extend our affordable housing tax credit and limit rent increases on mobile homes and update permitting to make housing development easier. These laws also took effect this week. We can never do enough to create more housing, but we're doing everything we can.

The Supplemental Budget maintains the state's obligation to pay 55 percent of basic local education costs to help hold down property taxes, and it expands property tax relief for Maine people. The budget maintains access to health care and reproductive health care, and it provides funds for the Maine Veterans Homes.

The budget includes ongoing funding to track forensic sexual assault examination kits, as well as permanent funding for domestic violence and sexual assault services, especially in the face of federal cuts. Other new laws will make it easier to report suspected neglect and abuse of older adults in Maine, and they will extend our childcare affordability programs, expand our nation-leading free school meals program, and help people purchase locally grown food to support our farmers.

My guiding belief as governor has always been that our strongest asset is you, the people of Maine. And that's why these new laws, especially the Supplemental Budget, do invest in you and support you and your families.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Section 18, Home and Community Based Services for Adults with Brain Injury Rate: Additional Services Identified for Removal of Service Provider Tax (SPT) CR 141031

Aug 06, 2026

Effective August 1, 2026, MaineCare updated certain Section 18 reimbursement rates to reflect the removal of the SPT, in alignment with P.L. 2023, Chapter 412, Part XXX. Please see our September 2024 e-message for more information. 

The services listed below were mistakenly overlooked when the Department originally identified documented add-on amounts associated with the SPT.

 

Procedure Code

Modifier

Code Description

Unit of Service

Rate Ending 7/31/2026

Rate Effective 8/1/2026

Home Support (Residential Habilitation) Level III - Increased Neurobehavioral, 2-4 Beds

Per Diem

$665.04

$627.40

T2016

U9 TG TT

Home Support (Residential Habilitation) Level III - Increased Neurobehavioral, 5-8 Beds

The full fee schedule is available on the Rate Setting page of the Health PAS Online Portal.

 

Adjustment Billing Guidance for Dates of Service August 1, 2026 – August 6, 2026

  • Providers are responsible for adjusting claims submitted with charges below the new rates. Per policy, and to avoid timely filing denials, adjustments must be submitted within 120 days of the most recent claim payment date.  

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

entry.content:

  • Help |
  • Search Maine.gov

DHHS → Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) → Provider Resources → Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) Clinical Eligibility Review and Billing Criteria for Section 45 and 46 Hospitals Update

Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) Clinical Eligibility Review and Billing Criteria for Section 45 and 46 Hospitals Update

Aug 10, 2026

Beginning September 1, 2026, IOP services delivered by hospitals enrolled under MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Chapter II, Sections 45 and 46 will require clinical eligibility review and billing criteria in alignment with Medicare’s IOP services billing requirements.  

Effective for dates of service on, or after, September 1, 2026, hospitals delivering IOP services must: 

  1. Submit a clinical review request to Acentra Health before delivering services to determine a MaineCare member’s IOP service eligibility. Members determined to meet clinical eligibility criteria as defined in MBM, Chapter II, Section 65 will receive a Case ID number to authorize billing for the delivery of IOP services by Section 45 and 46 providers. 

  2. With clinical review approval, deliver IOP services in accordance with their hospital licensure and the requirements of MBM, Chapter II, Section 65.05-4.  

  3. Submit claims using the corresponding CPT/HCPCS codes or revenue codes for actual services delivered including modifier(s) as applicable. Condition Code 92 (CC 92) is required in Form Locator fields 18-24. 

  4. Retain the clinical review Case ID number in the member’s medical record. Because IOP services without a clinical review Case ID are not eligible for reimbursement, providers must maintain clinical review approval records for Program Integrity purposes. 

  5. Deliver services in accordance with Division of Licensing and Certification (DLC) requirements.   

Please note: This notice supersedes previous MaineCare Section 45 and 46 IOP billing instructions including, but not limited to, the June 14, 2023 and August 18, 2023 messages.  

Medicare’s claims criteria are outlined in the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publication, including MLN 13496 – Billing Requirements for Intensive Outpatient Program Services with New Condition Code 92.

For questions regarding hospital licensure requirements for the delivery of IOP services, please reach out to Anna Blackwell, Associate Director of DLC: Medical Facilities Unit.  

For questions regarding IOP service and eligibility standards set forth in Section 65, or the billing requirements for providers enrolled under Sections 45 and 46, please contact Provider Relations Specialist Tiffany Norton.

entry.content:

DHHS → Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) → Provider Resources → Single Assessment Timing Requirements Reminder

Single Assessment Timing Requirements Reminder

Aug 11, 2026

The summary below outlines the timing requirements for initial and repeat Single Assessments, including the limited exceptions to the standard annual assessment cycle for children receiving medium- and high-intensity behavioral health services.

 

Situation

When is a Single Assessment Required?

Timing

Child already receiving services (no prior Single Assessment)

If the child has never had a Single Assessment, complete one before the next authorization is issued. After that, follow the standard annual reassessment schedule.

Before the next authorization (typically at the next Continued Stay Review (CSR)), then every 12 months

New request for medium- or high-intensity services

Complete a Single Assessment before submitting the initial referral or authorization request.

Initial assessment

Child continues receiving medium- or high-intensity services

Repeat the Single Assessment to confirm ongoing eligibility. Continue submitting CSRs between annual assessments.

Every 12 months

Child residing in a Children’s Residential Care Facility (CRCF)

Complete a Single Assessment when discharge planning begins to determine eligibility for community-based services after discharge.

At discharge planning

On a CRCF wait list

Repeat the Single Assessment while the child remains on the wait list.

Every 6 months

Child receiving services that began before the Single Assessment process was implemented

If no Single Assessment has been completed and the current authorization is nearing expiration, complete an initial Single Assessment before the next authorization. After that, follow the annual reassessment schedule.

At the first CSR after Single Assessment implementation, then every 12 months thereafter.

 

For questions, please contact Karen Sax-McLoughlin, Principal Settlement Manager at the Office of Behavioral Health.

Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) applications Open today, Friday, August 14

August 14, 2026

The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) is opening applications for the Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) today, Friday, August 14, 2026.

Maine farmers, forestry businesses, aquaculture producers, and other eligible producers who experienced weather-related losses in 2023 or 2024 may qualify for financial assistance.

Eligible losses may include crop loss, aquaculture loss, standing timber loss, harvested timber loss, on-farm and forestry infrastructure loss, and bare-ground practices necessary to mitigate land loss.

Application period: August 14, 2026, through November 6, 2026.

Applications will be accepted through the online portal. Paper applications are available upon request.

Producers can prepare now. Applicants are encouraged to begin gathering documentation, including:

  • Ownership or lease documentation
  • Parcel ID information
  • FSA Farm Number, if applicable
  • Tax or business identification information
  • Photos or records documenting damage

Other records related to weather-related losses in 2023 and/or 2024 DACF will provide technical assistance throughout the application period. Virtual office hours will be held every Friday from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. beginning August 14.

For updates, eligibility information, and application details, visit maine.gov/dacf/nrdrap, email NRDRA.DACF@maine.gov, or call (207) 530-3144.
